column3: Close to the Greek; BSB follows the critical text with “Christ Jesus” twice, without the Textus Receptus “Lord” in the second phrase.
BSB follows the critical text with “God the Father” without “our.”
BSB recasts the sentence: “you should stay on at Ephesus” supplies a main clause, and “false doctrines” renders “other doctrines.”
BSB adds “work” to “the stewardship of God”; “stewardship” follows the critical text (οἰκονομίαν), where the Textus Receptus reads “edification.”
BSB renders “good conscience” as “clear conscience.”
BSB starts a new sentence and adds “ways”; “from which” refers back to the things in verse 5.
BSB starts a new sentence (“They want”) and adds “but.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB renders “knowing this” as “We realize.”
Close to the Greek; “averse to” renders “opposed to.”
Close to the Greek; “glorious gospel” renders “the gospel of the glory.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB starts a new sentence and moves “because … unbelief” before “I was shown mercy”; “violent man” renders “insolent.”
BSB renders “surpassingly increased” as “overflowed” and adds “to me.”
Close to the Greek; “the worst” renders “foremost.”
BSB adds “of sinners” to “the worst.”
BSB follows the critical text with “the only God”; the Textus Receptus has “the only wise God.” “The King eternal” renders “the King of the ages.”
BSB moves “Timothy, my child” to the front; “fight the good fight” renders “wage the good warfare.”
Close to the Greek; “thereby shipwrecked their faith” renders “made shipwreck concerning the faith.”
BSB renders “be disciplined” as “be taught.”
